name: Platycerus oregonensis
intro: One pair produced approximately 13 larvae. One survived the summer and reached the third instar.

sections.title: Larvae
sections.text: The room repeatedly became hot during summer, when the other larvae died. I did not measure the peak temperature. As the room cooled, the survivor built a chamber, emptied its gut and became pale. It stayed there for months. By March its gut contained brown wood again and its body had a bluish cast. I left the chamber intact. The larva had resumed feeding without pupating.

facts.title: After a hot summer
facts.text: One survivor reached the third instar

sources.title: Alan Jeon, breeding and overwintering observation

account_credit: Breeding notes by Junkai Wang and Alan Jeon

distribution.caption: Paulsen and Caterino document this western stag beetle in British Columbia, Washington, Oregon and California.
distribution.alt: Documented regions for Platycerus oregonensis: British Columbia, California, Oregon, Washington.
